features.name: Rebuild external skill provenance and update gate
features.description: Rebuild every external skills-lock entry from its live upstream, then make the weekly updater reject local external sources so ChatGPT marketplace publication has traceable supply-chain metadata.
features.evidence: Root cause found: setup.sh's per-skill restore heuristic in `register_skills()` string-matches the *new* value `npx skills add <local-dir>` just wrote, but `npx` always resolves to the latest published `skills` package at run time — a version drift silently changed how it serializes a local path (e.g. no './' prefix), and the very next weekly run then clobbered every external skill's source/sourceType to local in one shot (confirmed via git history: PR #4 on 2026-07-28 introduced 65 local entries; every subsequent weekly sync perpetuated it since the drift-check step recomputes its 'expected github' baseline from the same already-corrupted file, so it always found nothing to flag). Fixed skills-lock.json by rebuilding all 65 corrupted entries from live upstream via `npx skills` (verified against last-known-good commit 7a35f06's parent — 0 mismatches). Fixed update-external-skills.yml: added a pre-run snapshot step and a new 'Force-restore upstream source/sourceType/skillPath' step that unconditionally overwrites those three fields from the pre-run snapshot for every skill that was sourceType==github before the run, keyed by exact JSON key — independent of whatever setup.sh/npx produced, so this class of bug can no longer slip through regardless of npx version behavior. Verified the jq merge logic against both a synthetic clean case and the real historical corrupted state. ./init.sh passes.
